---
title: Typst format
---

## Overview

`typst` output renders your document with [Typst](https://typst.app), a
modern typesetting system, and produces a PDF. It's an alternative to
`pdf` (LaTeX) worth considering when you want fast compiles and don't need
LaTeX-specific packages.

Rendering to `typst` requires a `typst` binary. Quarto does not bundle
one — install it from [typst.app](https://typst.app) and make sure it's on
your `PATH`, or point the `QUARTO_TYPST` environment variable at wherever
it lives. Quarto requires `typst` 0.8 or newer.

## Basic usage

Render a single document to `typst` from the command line:

``` bash
quarto render document.qmd --to typst
```

Or set it as the document's format in the YAML front matter:

``` {.yaml filename="document.qmd"}
---
title: "My Document"
format: typst
---
```

Either way, the output is a PDF — the intermediate Typst source Quarto
generates along the way is deleted once the compile succeeds (see
`keep-typ` below if you want to keep it).

## Format options

Set these under `format: typst:` in your document or project YAML.

### Multi-column layout

``` {.yaml filename="document.qmd"}
format:
  typst:
    columns: 2
```

### Custom template

Typst output is built from a Quarto-provided template. Point `template`
at your own `.typ` file to override it:

``` {.yaml filename="document.qmd"}
format:
  typst:
    template: my-template.typ
```

Your template can still reference Quarto's own template partials (for
example the numbering and page-geometry helpers) — they're staged
alongside it, not replaced.

### PDF standard

Typst can target a specific PDF/A or PDF/UA conformance level via
`pdf-standard`:

``` {.yaml filename="document.qmd"}
format:
  typst:
    pdf-standard: "a-2b"
```

Accepts either a single value or an array (e.g. `["2.0", "a-2b"]`). An
unrecognized standard is dropped with a warning rather than passed
through to `typst` verbatim.

### Keeping the intermediate Typst source

Quarto deletes the intermediate `.typ` file after a successful compile.
Set `keep-typ: true` to keep it alongside the PDF — useful if you want to
inspect or hand-edit the generated Typst source:

``` {.yaml filename="document.qmd"}
format:
  typst:
    keep-typ: true
```

## Cross-references and numbering

Figures, tables, equations, and other cross-referenced elements are
numbered natively by Typst's own compiler, not by Quarto — the same
`@fig-`/`@tbl-`/`@eq-` syntax you use for every other format works as
expected, and the numbers Typst prints always match the numbers your
`@ref`s resolve to.

## Margin notes

Content placed in a `column-margin` div (or referenced via margin
citations) renders in the page margin, using Typst's
[marginalia](https://typst.app/universe/package/marginalia) package,
which Quarto vendors and stages automatically — no extra installation
step required:

``` markdown
Body text with a reference to the margin.[^note]

::: {.column-margin}
This appears in the margin next to the paragraph above.
:::
```

## brand.yml support

`typst` output honors your project's [`_brand.yml`](/guides/authoring/brand.qmd)
for colors and typography, the same way other formats do.

## Packages beyond the ones Quarto vendors

Quarto vendors a handful of Typst packages its own template and Lua
filters depend on (including `marginalia` for margin notes). If your
document's own Typst content references an additional
[Typst Universe](https://typst.app/universe) package via `#import
"@preview/..."` — for example inside a raw Typst block — Quarto detects
that reference and fetches the package automatically before compiling,
the first time it's needed.
